summary: Reconciler hygiene consumes an independent S4 cursor, processes only changed eligible open issues, expands parent changes to children in the feed snapshot, and preserves timer work. Pending empty-audit candidates retain grace work without unchanged comment rereads. Sweeps serialize and publish exactly their pre-work cursor only after every candidate succeeds. Unsupported tracking uses the full prior path; startup/history gaps reseed.
public_interfaces: BeadsAdvanced::hygiene_changes(Option<&HygieneCursor>) -> Result<Option<HygieneBatch>>: default returns None; Err remains retryable
internal_interfaces: S4 feed version 3: structural OLD/NEW children and replacement victims advance issue_revision only
IssueReads::hygiene shares the persistent reader connection, with caller-owned independent cursor
Reconciler::hygiene mutex holds HygieneState { cursor, pending }; staged publication is cancellation-safe
Indexed parent-to-child expansion precedes open filtering; parent IDs avoid graph snapshots on supported deltas

solvers.bindings: Staged snapshot before work; failure preserves old state; success publishes staged cursor; before-grace remains pending; concurrent write leaves later feed work; gap resets. Core conservatively invalidates any reported issue/comment/parent change, a stricter policy than the membership reuse predicate.
solvers.caveats: Declared finite models assume complete change coverage and correct identity/filter mapping. They do not prove Rust, all SQL triggers/interleavings, unbounded liveness, memory byte bounds or runtime savings.
solvers.validation_note: Initial post workflow request lacked required target_states and was rejected before solving; corrected to Checked, with unchanged rules and trace.

limitations: Hygiene cursor is in memory; restart reseeds.
Concurrent writes converge on later sweeps; no atomic comments-plus-label-repair transaction was added.
Partial failures replay the whole unacknowledged batch, including earlier successful repairs.
Pending state is proportional to eligible grace-pending candidates; no TTL or arbitrary cap.
No live binary changes or notebook profiling performed; S7 owns final integrated profiling and measured runtime savings.
